name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,398

clue.text: Pamper group on Greek island

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another means it follows it in the row

blocks.note: Kos, also spelt Cos, is an island in the Aegean
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A holiday group being spoilt on a sunny Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset someone is to indulge and fuss over them, a direct synonym of pamper.

clue.text: Game lacking a new style is worthless

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named letters are dropped

blocks.note: canasta is a rummy-style card game
the letter to drop, taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new; also dropped
a way of doing something is a style or manner

explanation.surface: A game played without any fresh approach is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Canasta is a rummy-style card game; 'lacking a new' removes exactly one A and the N, leaving its other A in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Castaway as an adjective means discarded or rejected, so something thrown away as being worthless.

clue.text: Rigid objections brought up and almost tolerated

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up means it reads from the bottom upwards
almost means not quite, so the last letter is missing

blocks.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
borne means endured or put up with

explanation.surface: Firm objections raised in a meeting and only just put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is rigid and inflexible, refusing to change their mind or position.

clue.text: I've noted down wine that is lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, a lifted word is raised so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: red is a colour of wine
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone noting down which wine was raised in a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the eider speaks of itself as famous, or noted, for its down. 'Noted down' looks like writing something down.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider duck is well known for the soft breast feathers used to fill eiderdown quilts.

clue.text: Area with clubs a couple snubbed possibly in Mexican resort

indicators.note: to snub originally means to cut short, so the word loses its tail
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be put in another order

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area
C stands for clubs, the card suit
taken as written before trimming and rearranging

explanation.surface: A couple shunned by the clubs crowd at a Mexican beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A COUPLE loses its last letter to leave ACOUPL, which is then rearranged as APULCO after A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a famous Pacific beach resort city on the coast of Mexico.

clue.text: One professionally managing issue?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose job is handling a problem or matter
setter's reading: issue meaning offspring, so the job is looking after other people's children

explanation.walkthrough: Issue sounds like a business problem, but in law and old usage it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a paid carer who looks after other people's young children in their own home.

clue.text: Footballer, one stopping rubbish defensive error by defender (missing second half)

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap from inside, so one piece is lodged within the other
the back half of the word is absent, so only its front half remains

blocks.note: pulp is trashy, worthless stuff, as in pulp fiction
A means one, the indefinite article
OG is an own goal, a defender's mistake in football
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: A footballer blocking a rubbish defensive error made by a team-mate.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal is the classic error by a defender; 'second half' of the defender's word means its last two letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Pogba is a French international midfielder who played for Manchester United and Juventus.

clue.text: Face maybe being confined to bed?

blocks.note: first meaning: a playing card, say, set down face upwards on the table
second meaning: kept in bed by illness or injury

explanation.walkthrough: Face looks like the front of the head, but it is the face of a card, put down showing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a card placed face upwards, and is also an idiom for someone ill and kept to their bed.

clue.text: Work Frenchman took up in introduction

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman taking on work at the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is the first item or move that begins something, much like an introduction.

clue.text: Robust rule observed in musical composition

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a study, or étude, is a piece written to practise a technique
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A strict rule followed in the writing of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy and robust are synonyms, both describing something strongly built and hard to damage.

clue.text: Some seconds include principally ices and trifles

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so only the chief or leading letters are taken
to include something is to take it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a minute is made up of sixty seconds
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A dessert menu of ices and trifles served in a matter of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of ices and and go inside MINUTE, between its T and E. 'Trifles' looks like the pudding but means small details.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, trivial details, just as trifles are matters of little importance.

clue.text: Possible follower of Green, largely blooming as a politician

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so not quite the whole word is kept

blocks.note: on British traffic lights, amber comes after green
ruddy means rosy and healthy-looking, like a blooming complexion

explanation.surface: A Green Party candidate's successor flourishing in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Green looks like the political party but refers to the traffic light. RUDDY loses its last letter. Amber Rudd was a Conservative Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber Rudd served as a Conservative Member of Parliament and cabinet minister in Britain.

clue.text: Tone of extremist Republican in US state

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an ultra is a political extremist
Maine is the north-eastern US state
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: The tone adopted by a hardline Republican politician in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Tone looks like a manner of speaking, but it is a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultramarine is a deep, vivid blue shade, so it is a colour tone used by painters.

clue.text: Early signs of po-faced reactions usually display existence - of one?

definitions.text: Early signs of po-faced reactions usually display existence - of one?

indicators.note: the earliest sign of each word is its opening letter, so only those are taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Disapproving, stony-faced reactions as the telltale signs of a certain sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a disapproving, prim face is how one of these people reacts to anything risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: A prude is easily shocked by impropriety, and typically shows it with a disapproving, po-faced look.

clue.text: Cook snaring port - part of cook's habit?

indicators.note: to cook up is to concoct or doctor, so the letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook trapping a glass of port, with a hint about what cooks wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' appears twice: first as the anagram signal, then in the definition as the person in the kitchen. Habit here means clothing, not routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron string ties the apron a cook wears, so it is part of the cook's working dress, or habit.

clue.text: Piece worthy to be heard? It makes one restless

indicators.note: being heard means listened to rather than read, so the spelling follows the spoken sound

blocks.note: a knight is a chess piece
a worthy is a local dignitary, such as a mayor

explanation.surface: A worthwhile piece of writing that is meant to be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: Worthy looks like an adjective, but as a noun it means a local notable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream disturbs sleep and leaves the sleeper troubled, unable to rest easily.

clue.text: First off, big man, say, trained here?

definitions.text: First off, big man, say, trained here?

indicators.note: with the first taken off, the opening letter is dropped
training reshapes something, so the letters are put into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written before the first letter is lost
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Where a big man, for example, might have done his training.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a big, muscular man is likely to have trained in a gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasia, the Latin plural of gymnasium, are halls where people exercise and build strength.

clue.text: Coroner ordered date to be officially acknowledged

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A coroner sets the date for an inquest to be formally recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on record has been formally documented, so it is officially acknowledged and noted.

clue.text: With sum of money, minister tours variable tourist attraction

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars
a canon is a member of the clergy, a minister of the church
Y is a letter used for a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A well-paid clergyman on a tour of different sights.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, x, y and z are the usual letters for variables, so 'variable' can stand for any of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is one of the most visited natural sights in the United States.

clue.text: What's soothing about hot yoga ultimately in London suburb

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken
about means around, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A soothing hot-yoga class in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: H and A go inside BALM, between its L and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Balham is a residential district of south London, in the borough of Wandsworth.

clue.text: Problem over short outrageous heading

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes
in a down clue, one piece over another is written above it

blocks.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in there's the rub
rich can mean outrageous or preposterous, as in that's rich

explanation.surface: A problem summed up in a brief, outrageous headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading or title in a book, originally one written in red ink.

clue.text: Figure that's beyond a minority?

blocks.note: surface reading: a number bigger than a small share of a group
setter's reading: minority as the legal state of being under age, so a person past it

explanation.walkthrough: Minority suggests a smaller group, but it is also the period of being legally a child; figure means a person, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up person has passed the age of majority, leaving the legal state of minority behind.

clue.text: A classic car with which old French director shows conceit

blocks.note: taken as written
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury car
O is a standard abbreviation for old
Abel Gance was a French film director, maker of Napoléon (1927)

explanation.surface: An old French film-maker showing off with a vintage motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance and conceit are both an excessive sense of one's own importance or worth.

clue.text: Repellent drug, an ingrained phenomenon

blocks.note: grim means unpleasant or repellent
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A repulsive drug habit that has become deeply rooted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingrained looks like a deep-rooted habit, but it is literally dirt worked into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is dirt that has worked deep into a surface, so it is characteristically ingrained.

clue.text: Retired volunteers engaged in complex computing etc are very busy

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word goes backwards
being engaged in something means being caught up inside it, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: hard means difficult or complicated
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
IT is information technology, computing and the like

explanation.surface: Retired volunteers immersed in complicated computer work, busy as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, a staple crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hard at it is an idiom for working energetically, matching the plural phrase are very busy.

clue.text: Mafia's constructed casing for bomb

indicators.note: a casing is an outer shell, so the words wrap around the letters wanted

blocks.note: found inside these words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A Mafia bomb assembled inside a casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casing for bomb' reads like explosives, but bomb is the definition in its sense of a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that bombs is a total failure, and a fiasco is a humiliating, complete failure.

clue.text: One in school with coat before start of lesson

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: a mack, or mackintosh, is a raincoat
ere is an old word for before
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A pupil putting on a raincoat before the first class begins.
explanation.walkthrough: School suggests a classroom, but it is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mackerel swim in large shoals, also called schools, so each fish is one member of a school.

clue.text: Cartoonist, maybe, about to get prize

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a cartoonist is one example of someone who draws

explanation.surface: A cartoonist about to collect an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition of achievement, just as a prize is.
